title: The altar of witness (Joshua 22)
hookLine: a misunderstood altar nearly starts a war, until people talk

lines: A GREAT ALTAR BY THE JORDAN.
cards: The soldiers are finally going home. For a long time the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh have fought beside everyone else, though their own land lies east of the Jordan.
Joshua blesses them and sends them back across. At the river, they stop and build an altar. A big one, the text says, great to look at.
Word reaches the other tribes, and the whole congregation gathers at Shiloh for war. Brothers who just fought side by side are about to fight each other, over a pile of stones nobody has explained.

teach.h: A SECOND ALTAR LOOKS LIKE BETRAYAL.
teach.b: To the other tribes, it looks like betrayal. In the Torah, offerings belong at the one place God chooses, and here is a second altar, on the edge of the land.
They remember Peor, where the people strayed, and Achan, whose sin brought trouble on everyone, and they're afraid the whole people will pay again.
But before anyone draws a sword, they send people to talk: Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, with ten princes, one from each tribe.

They accuse, and they also offer: if your land feels unclean, come over and take a portion among us. The eastern tribes answer, beginning with God's names, said twice, as if under oath: God knows, and Israel shall know.
The altar was never meant for offerings. It was built out of fear. The Jordan runs between us, they say.
One day your children might tell our children, you have no portion in the Lord.

teach.h: WE BUILT IT SO OUR CHILDREN BELONG.
teach.b: So we built a copy of the altar, a witness between us, so our children can point at it and say, we belong too. Phinehas hears it, and the mood turns at once: this day we know the Lord is among us. The army goes home.
And the eastern tribes name the altar with a reason: "for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God." The Hebrew word for witness there is ed, and some translations call the altar Ed.
The altar that nearly started a war was built to keep a family together, and nobody knew until somebody asked.

how: Jews read Joshua 22 as part of the Former Prophets, and teachers often turn to it as a story about suspicion between communities and the conversation that ended it.

o: a border stone between the eastern tribes
a witness: the name of the altar by the Jordan
an offering burned on the altar by the river

games.q: talk before you fight — tap the pairs.
p: sent to talk before the war
the river they feared would divide them

s: the eastern tribes built the altar for their own offerings
they say it was never for offerings: it was a copy, built as a witness that they belong.
Israel sent a delegation before going to war
Phinehas and ten princes, one from each tribe, went to talk first.
the other tribes offered to share their own land
if your land feels unclean, come over and take a portion among us.

games.q: you're one of the tribes at Shiloh. your kin across the Jordan have built a great altar. everyone's arming for war. what do you do?
o: march at once, before it spreads.
send people across to ask what it means.
ignore it: it's their side of the river.
games.why: they send Phinehas and ten princes. the answer they hear, a witness so our children belong, ends the war before it starts.

practice: Bring to mind one thing someone did lately that you've been reading the worst way: a short message, a silence, a change of plans.

Notice the story you've already written about it, then write a second one, the way the eastern tribes explained their altar; you don't have to believe it, just hold both. Then shape one question you could ask.

wordCard.voice: Ed. The altar by the Jordan that looked like rebellion, turned out to be a plea to belong, and was named as a witness. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: witness. the word in Joshua 22:34; some translations call the altar Ed.
